All other 73 tests pass; the one failure confirms a genuine bug in the code, not the test.

## Summary

I added `src/test/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/math/NumberUtilsAgentTest.java`, a self-contained JUnit 5 test class (matching the project's JUnit version) covering `NumberUtils`'s constants, comparators, `create*` factory methods, `isCreatable`/`isNumber`/`isDigits`/`isParsable`, the `min`/`max` family (arrays and 3-arg overloads, across all primitive types, including null/empty-array errors and NaN propagation for `float`/`double`), the `to*` conversion-with-default methods (including numeric-overflow cases), and `toScaledBigDecimal`.

74 tests run, 73 pass. One fails and shows a real bug, which I left failing rather than adjusting:

- **`testCreateNumberLongSuffixWithLeadingPlusSign`** — `NumberUtils.createNumber("+123L")` throws `NumberFormatException: +123L is not a valid number.`, while the symmetric `NumberUtils.createNumber("-123L")` correctly returns `Long(-123)`. In `createNumber`'s `'L'/'l'` case, the guard only special-cases a leading `-` before calling `isDigits` on the remainder; it never does the same for a leading `+`, so a `+`-prefixed long literal is wrongly rejected.
